```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path.cwd() / "src"))
from lectures import plotting, datasets
from lectures.plotting import INK, COOL, WARM, CRASH, despine, annotate_box
from rbig import AnnealedRBIG
from lectures.measures import cocrash_fraction
plotting.set_style("notes")
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

*Do-the-job track · Job C of 3.*

Fit RBIG to real returns and run it **backward** to generate scenarios.  The
deliverable is a synthetic scenario set whose **joint tail** matches the real
data — the input every risk calculation needs.  (This is the bridge to
[Uncertainty](../../uncertainty/index.qmd).)

---

## 1 · Fit on a Real Sub-Basket

```{python}
R = datasets.load_returns()
assets = ["JPM", "BAC", "XOM"]
X = R[assets].to_numpy()
X = (X - X.mean(0)) / X.std(0)
print(f"fitting RBIG on {assets}, {len(X)} days")

rbig = AnnealedRBIG(n_layers=30, random_state=0).fit(X)
gen = rbig.sample(4000)
```

## 2 · Do the Scenarios Match the Real Tail?

```{python}
print(f"{'pair':<10}{'real co-crash':>14}{'generated':>11}")
print("-" * 35)
pairs = [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2)]
for i, j in pairs:
    cr = cocrash_fraction(X[:, i], X[:, j])
    cg = cocrash_fraction(gen[:, i], gen[:, j])
    print(f"{assets[i]}/{assets[j]:<6}{cr:>14.0%}{cg:>11.0%}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-jobC-scenarios
#| fig-cap: "Real returns (left) and RBIG-generated scenarios (right) for the JPM/BAC pair — same bulk and same lower-tail co-crash."
fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, data, col, title in [
    (axL, X, COOL, f"real · co-crash {cocrash_fraction(X[:,0], X[:,1]):.0%}"),
    (axR, gen, WARM, f"generated · co-crash {cocrash_fraction(gen[:,0], gen[:,1]):.0%}"),
]:
    ax.scatter(data[:, 0], data[:, 1], s=7, c=col, alpha=0.3, edgecolors="none")
    ax.axvspan(-8, np.quantile(data[:, 0], 0.1), color=CRASH, alpha=0.06)
    ax.axhspan(-8, np.quantile(data[:, 1], 0.1), color=CRASH, alpha=0.06)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xlim(-6, 5); ax.set_ylim(-6, 5)
    ax.set_xlabel("JPM (z)"); ax.set_ylabel("BAC (z)")
    despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## The Deliverable
A scenario matrix you can feed to any portfolio function.  Unlike independent
resampling (which destroys the co-crash) or a Gaussian Monte-Carlo (which thins
the tail), these scenarios carry the *real* joint extremes — see
[Uncertainty · noise and propagation](../../uncertainty/03-noise-and-propagation.qmd).
:::
